I present to you this petition in order that, when you have visited the spot and observed her (?) condition, Joanna may be secured until the result

berkeley:230748.c: Official letter in which one official informs another about the disappearance of a number of hides.

berkeley:230749.t: P.Tebt., III.802. Petition to the hipparches.
berkeley:230749.c: Paalas petitions the hipparches, complaining that certain people had damaged his ship and assaulted himself. ; Translation: The 36th year, Hathur 11. To Demetrios, one of the diadochoi, hipparches over men and epistates, from Paalas son of Harmais, ship's guard of the barge of Apollonios, one of the first friends and strategos and overseer of the revenues. berkeley:230750.t: P.Tebt., III.803. Petition to the Hipparches
berkeley:230750.c: The Crown tenants of Oxyrhyncha petition the hipparches, mentioning a great reduction in their number by various acts of injustice. ; Translation: To Aminias, one of the diadochoi, hipparches and epistates of Oxyrhyncha, from the Crown cultivators of the said village. Whereas we were formerly 140 men but because of the injustices done to us are 40 in all, although ... (Here the papyrus breaks off.)

berkeley:230751.c: Petition to the epistates of Tebtunis, reporting the burglary of a house. ; Translation: To Poseidonios, epistates of Tebtunis, from Pa[--] son of Pasis, cultivator from the said village. On the night preceding the 5th of Phamenoth of the 5th year certain persons forced their way into my house and having undermined the doorpost entered the vestibule. I woke up and shouted for help ... (Here the papyrus breaks off.)

berkeley:230753.t: P.Tebt., III.843, lines 1-10. Register of land
berkeley:230753.c: Part of an account concerning crown land. ; Translation: … land leased for copper money by Chairemon, one of the diadochi and epimeletes, 390 1/16 1/32 arouras, of which 30 arouras belong to the land leased for grain, yielding, at 1 artaba, 30 artabas, the remainder being 360 1/16 1/32 ar., of which there is a lease till the 28th year to Dionysios at a total for the nome of 1 talent 4500 drachmas of copper.

berkeley:230754.t: P.Tebt., III.805; Hengstl, Griechische Papyri, no. 126. Petition to the komarches.

I leased to Petesouchos son of Teos, an inhabitant of the said village, out of the Crown land which I cultivate at the village 3 1/4 1/8 arouras for the 4th year at a rent per aroura of 5 talents of bronze, on condition that he should sow it with garlic, by an Egyptian contract of lease, having agreed with him that he should pay before the 30th

berkeley:230755.c: Eutychos declares his horse to the basilikos grammateus. ; Translation: To N.N. basilikos grammateus, from Eutychos son of Eutychos, Acarnanian of the 100-arouras-holders of Demetrios and his sons in the 4th hipparchy. I return the chestnut female horse that belongs to me. Let this return be placed on record for me, in order that I may not subsequently be calumniated. Farewell. The 31st year, Mesore 21. (2nd hand) … The 31st year, Mesore 23.

I learn from several persons that Petous … komarches of the village, is defaulting and misconducting himself, and that he is greatly in arrears with the amount agreed on with him and due for his appointment, … [artabas] of grain, and has deferred it up to the 20th of …, being in debt for more than half. Hasten therefore … (Addressed on the verso) To the harvest-guards and cultivators at Oxyrhyncha.

berkeley:231482.c: Receipt for payment of beer-tax ; Translation: Year 10: Pharion, son of Patronos, paid in the month of Phamenoth for individual beer tax an additional 8 drachmai. It is 8 drachmai.

berkeley:231483.c: List of persons in which the names Zoilakouis, Panalais, Ponnis, and Panetumis occur.

berkeley:231484.t: P.Tebt., II.424; Hunt, A.S. Sel.pap., v. 1, no. 154; Tibiletti, G. Lettere private, no. 17. Private letter from Sarapammon : t Piperas : draft or copy
berkeley:231484.c: Sarapammon urges Piperas not to fool around any more because he has a large debt ; Translation: Sarapammon to Piperas. I sent you a letter by the baker, and perhaps you know what I wrote to you. If you persist in your folly, I congratulate you; if you repent, you only know. Let me tell you that you owe seven years' rents and dues, so unless you now send discharges you know your danger.

berkeley:231485.c: Receipt for an artaba of grain for the manufacture of beer ; Translation: parmouthi 23 ammonis, slave 1 artaba for beer

berkeley:231486.c: Taxes paid through Protas by Heron

berkeley:231487.c: Receipt for 15 silver drachmae issued to Anempsais

berkeley:231488.c: Receipt for 5 drachmae (?) paid to Kapiton, Son of Dionysios

berkeley:231489.c: Receipt for payment of 2 drachmae paid of Petesouchos son of Anempsais

berkeley:231490.c: Receipt goven to Petesouchos Son of Anempais, for taxes. ; Translation: Ammonios to Petesouchos, son of Anempsais, greeting. I have from you for the account of the epitritos for the 25th, in addition to the four (drachmai) of silver, another three (drachmai).

berkeley:231491.c: Receipt issued to Kopreas, for 40 desmai.

berkeley:231493.c: Receipt issued to Apollon, a slave, for two sacks.

berkeley:231495.t: P.Tebt., III.722. Order for payment to soldiers
berkeley:231495.c: Samios orders Herakleides to measure out grain for the infantry soldiers of the Arsinoite nome ; Translation: Samios to Herakleides, greeting. If the agents of Apollonios the sitologos are measuring grain in presence of the assessors, give them from the store at Boubastos to Hestieios the agent of Apollodoros, scribe, for the infantry, encamped in the nome, belonging to the Macedonian corps from which he writes (?), [.]3 artabas of wheat. Good-bye. [Date.]

berkeley:231504.t: P.Tebt., I.64 (a). Report on the crops of Kerkeosiris
berkeley:231504.c: Report on lands and crops at Kerkeosiris, including crops, cleruchic lists, different land classes, and crown and temple lands.

berkeley:231505.t: P.Tebt., II.342. Report on confiscated property
berkeley:231505.c: Report concerning the tenure of certain pieces of property in the Hermopolite nome. Their ownership was vested in the government, probably in some cases through confiscation. ; Translation: (Col. III) And the several plots in accordance with the survey-list presented in Hathyr of the 12th year by Noumenios the agent; that which was previously drawn up by Orpheus … Starting on the south of the southern road … adjoining on the east is the pottery formerly belonging to Lepton and leased to Tothes (according to an agreement made) in the 24th year which is also the 1st year …, of which it was repor

berkeley:231506.t: P.Tebt., I.153. Register of the crops of crown lands
berkeley:231506.c: Fragment of a register of the various crops grown on crown lands at Kerkeosiris in an unknown year, with a statement of rents due to the crown.

berkeley:231510.c: The name of the deceased appears in Greek script on one side, in Egyptian Demotic script on the other. Pakoumis is the transliterated and declined Greek for the Egyptian name meaning "The eagle." The man's patronymic, given in the Greek genitive as Pantbooutos, is an Egyptian name meaning "The one of the avenging demons." Unlike the Greek side, the Egyptian also gives the name of the grandfather of Pakoumis, P3j-ht (He of the ht-Daimon)

berkeley:231511.t: P.Tebt., II.295. Register of priestly offices
berkeley:231511.c: A statement concerning certain priestly offices at Tebtunis, which also record earlier history for bidding for the post of prophetes ; Translation: (Lines 2-12) Priestly offices: those stated by Claudius Dionysios, the former strategos, to have been reported to him by his predecessor Charisios to have been reported to Charisios himself by his predecessor Apollonides as requiring to be sold, include the post of prophet of the temple of Soknebtynis also called Kronos at the village of Tebtunis, for which it was stated that a first offer of 100 drachmas was made by Harpokration son of Marepsemis,

berkeley:231512.c: Horos and the elders of the farmers petition to Menches complaining about an attack that hindered them in their work.

berkeley:231514.c: Fragment of a register of land, giving a list of persons leasing land and the rents paid. ; Translation: and with Hermes and Ares, ring-makers…measurers, key-makers, utensil-crafters, and with…cooks, bakers, preparers (?) …being added to... …potters, and if even Dios[kouroi (?)... …and with Kronos, linen-weavers, hair-[dressers?]…embroiderers, hierophants …Ares [produces?] barbers (?), hair-dressers (epimeletas)... …cobblers, stitchers, cloak-makers (himatio[poious]?)... …and with Zeus and Helios shining golden (chryso[poi]?)... …of master-builders... …and of Ares for public... on the one hand

berkeley:231515.c: Includes entries about ships, soldiers, animals, plants, and seller of …

berkeley:231520.t: P.Tebt., I.1; C.Ord.Ptol., no. 53 bis; Plate: C.Ord.Ptol., fig. 1. Decrees of King Ptolemy VIII Euergetes II : copy
berkeley:231520.c: Commencement of the decrees of Ptolemy VIII Euergetes II.

berkeley:231521.t: P.Tebt., I.5; C.Ord.Ptol., no. 53; Plate: P.Tebt., I, pl. III (col. IX). Decrees of King Ptolemy VIII Euergetes II
berkeley:231521.c: Decrees copied by the village scribe of Kerkeosiris. Topics include constitutional innovations, corruption, government officials, administration of crown lands, safeguards to prevent tax fraud, and treatment of the people by officials ; Translation: (lines 1-13) King Ptolemaios and Queen Kleopatra the sister and Queen Kleopatra the wife proclaim an amnesty to all their subjects for errors, crimes, accusations, condemnations and charges of all kinds up to the 9th of Pharmouthi of the 52nd year, except to persons guilty of wilful murder or sacrilege. And they have decreed that persons who have g

berkeley:231522.t: P.Tebt., II.330; Chrest. Mitt., no. 110. Petition of Ptolemaios
berkeley:231522.c: Ptolemaios petitions Bolanos about a burglary of his house. ; Translation: To Bolanos, strategos of the divisions of Themistos and Polemon of the Arsinoite nome, from Ptolemaios son of Patron, of the village of Tebtunis. After being absent, when I returned to the village, I found my house pillaged and every thing that was stored in it carried off. Wherefore, being unable to submit to this, I apply to you and ask that this petition may be entered on the register in order that, if any one is proved to be the culprit, he may be held accountable to me. Farewell.

berkeley:231523.t: P.Tebt., III.763. Letter from Ptolemaios to Ptollis
berkeley:231523.c: Ptolemaios addresses Ptollis about some unclear business concerning a certain Diphilos and silver vessels. ; Translation: Ptolemaios to Ptollis, greeting. I have detained the letters about the affair of Diphilos in case an application may have been made to you, but if an application has still not been made, find out exactly where he says that he found them and state the silver vessels in clear writing, for one should not write incoherently about that kind of thing. Good-bye. (Addressed on the verso) To Ptollis.

berkeley:231524.c: Psyphis registers the birth of his son Pakebkis, born in the 10th year of Claudius (49/50 A.D.) with Areios, village scribe of Tebtunis. ; Translation: To Areios son of Lysimachos, komogrammateus of Tebtunis, from Psyphis son of Harpokras son of Pakebkis, his mother being Thenmarsisouchos daughter of Psyphis and Kellauthis, inhabitants of the village, priest of the fifth tribe of the gods at the village, Kronos the most great god, and Isis and Serapis, the great gods, and one of the fifty exempted persons. I register Pakebkis, the son born to me and Taaseies daughter of N.N. her mother being T

berkeley:231527.t: P.Tebt.Frag.14,190+14,202+14,234+14,321+14,324. Declation of names of people living in a household.
berkeley:231527.c: Sculptor and Mastmaker and their families and apprentices?

berkeley:231528.c: Account of expenses mentioning small amounts for women and men. Frags. 14,261 and 14,263 (?) give overview of account.

berkeley:231529.c: Apparently account of expenses. Frag. 14,235 gives overview of account.

berkeley:231530.t: P.Tebt., II.361. Receipt for land tax
berkeley:231530.c: A receipt for the land tax known as arithmetikon, paid by Protous to Didas and his partners. ; Translation: The sixteenth year of Imperator Caesar Trajanus Hadrianus Augustus, Payni 20. Paid to Didas and his partners, collectors at Tebtunis by Protous son of Areios for the full arithmetikon of the 16th year, 28 drachmas 3 obols. Total 28 dr. 3 ob., for extra charges 1 dr. 5 ob., for the receipt 3 ob.

berkeley:231531.c: Beginning of an account of the expenses in connection with the death of the writer's husband.

berkeley:231532.c: An account of payments in drachmae for stone masons, painters, plumbers, and other workmen along the Nile; followed by a writing exercise (in a different hand, in opposite direction).

berkeley:231533.c: Harphaesis petitions to Menches, complaining of an assault

berkeley:231534.c: Account of staters and drachmas of payments for annona (annual revenues in kind for civil and military purposes) and other items. ; Translation: Account of the expenditure (?) of 130 staters, on account of annona for grain and barley 16 staters, on account of grain and barley 32 staters and 2 drachmas, on account of a cow for annona 15 staters, on account of kids for annona 27 staters, on account of pigs for annona 30 staters; on account of the didrachms 67 staters, on account of the hunters (?) 30 arouras, 30 staters.

berkeley:231535.t: P.Tebt., I.16 recto (desc. only); P.Tebt. IV.1143. Account of payments in kind
berkeley:231535.c: List of persons required to pay a charge of 1/2 artaba (ca. 20 liters), followed by the names of four farmers of crown land, possibly at Kerkeosiris, Egypt.

berkeley:231539.t: P.Tebt., I.53 (desc. only). Account of Payments
berkeley:231539.c: Account of payments by an unknown person, for oil, wine, bread, etc., made from the 2nd to the 16th of an unknown month.

berkeley:231544.c: Census declaration made by Achilleus for seven persons living in a house in the Moeris quarter of that town. ; Translation: (6th h.) I, Apollonios also called Diogenes, have signed. (1st h.) To Ammonios, strategos of the division of Herakleides of the Arsinoite nome, and Harpokration also called Hierax, Basilikos Grammateus of the same division, and Mysthes and Heron, ex-scribes of the metropolis, from Achilleus son of Apollonios son of Lourios also called Apollonios, enrolled as a Katoikos, and already registered through another memorandum. I own in the Moeris quarter a share of a house and a

berkeley:231545.t: P.Tebt., II.278; Cribiore, R. Writing, Teachers, and Students in Graeco-Roman Egypt, no. 99 with plate (Pl. XI). Acrostics
berkeley:231545.c: A pair of acrostics, the first dealing with various artificers, the second with the loss of a garment. ; Translation: (Col. I) Baker, dyer, fuller, spear-maker, oilman, painter, cobbler, breastplate-maker, doctor, locksmith, mason, millstone-maker, shipwright, scraper-maker, armourer, tablet-maker, …, engraver, glassworker, … goldsmith, ... (Col. II) My (garment?) is lost; violent was he (who took it?), well-born was he who took it. It was bought for ten staters; if it had been a cloak I should not have minded. I seek but do not find it. It was taken without cause. He will meet with anger. Jus

berkeley:231546.t: P.Tebt., III.747. Agathon's official letter : To Patron
berkeley:231546.c: Agathon strongly rebukes Patron for neglect of his orders. Both probably hold posts in the Oxyrhynchite Nome. ; Translation: Agathon to Patron, greeting. You are the one and only person who entirely neglects our pressing commands. For though we have written to you and given you orders concerning the timber, you have paid no heed, but have delayed until Ammonios is annoyed and we have been forced to buy timber to send to him. I have written therefore to you in order that you may realize your own carelessness. Goodbye. The fourth year, Payni 11.

berkeley:231548.t: P.Tebt., III.746. Agathon's offical letter : to Patron
berkeley:231548.c: Agathon forwards to Patron a copy of the letter he received from Menodoros, an official. This letter includes a copy of a letter to Theophilos, giving instructions concerning the collection of dues upon the holdings of cavalry-soldiers. ; Translation: Agathon to Patron, greeting. I have written below for your information a copy of the letter from Menodoros. Goodbye. The 4th year, Pharmouthi 8. Menodoros to Agathon, greeting. We have written below for you a copy of the letter which we have written to the collectors in the several toparchies in order that you may be informed and send instruction

berkeley:231549.t: P.Tebt., III.745. Agathon's official letter : to Patron
berkeley:231549.c: Agathon, superior of Patron (personal name), requests Patron to hand over to Apollonios the position of guard. ; Translation: Agathon to Patron, greeting. Apollonios has applied to me about the village of Takona, that you should appoint him as guard. You would therefore do well to hand (the post?) over to him. Good-bye. The 2nd year, Mecheir 13. (Addressed on the verso) To Patron.

berkeley:231550.t: P.Tebt., III.748. Agathon's official letter : to Patron
berkeley:231550.c: Letter of Agathon to Patron (personal name) passing on to him instructions for procuring some animals for transport. ; Translation: Agathon to Patron, greeting. Ammonios has written to us to send him at the city beasts of burden for wagons, as the king is solicitous about them. Therefore on receipt of this letter go round your neighborhood with Zenodoros and send to the city any that you find ... (Addressed on the verso) To Patron. (Endorsed on the verso) Year . [month] 24. About draught-animals.

berkeley:231551.t: P.Tebt., III.749. Agathon's official letter : to Patron
berkeley:231551.c: Agathon writes to Patron (personal name) urging him to procure the best donkeys possible in the Arsinoite Nome.. ; Translation: Agathon to Patron, greeting. On receipt of my letter send a guard to the Arsinoite nome to get for us the best donkeys possible; do this quickly and send them to us at the city. Goodbye. (Addressed on the verso): To Patron.

berkeley:231552.t: P.Tebt., II.645; SB, XVIII, no. 13365. Penthemeros certificate
berkeley:231552.c: Certificate that Horos, son of Horos, has performed five days of dike corvee. ; Translation: Year four of Imperator Caesar Nerva Trajanus Augustus Germanicus. Has performed for five days for work on dikes for the same fourth year in the desert canal of Polemon, (2nd h.) on behalf of Tebtunis, Horos, son of Horos, grandson of N.N. (3rd h.) for Hermodoros, son of Isidoros, son of Herakles, his mother is Tap[- -]. (4th h.) I, Isidoros, have signed. (5th h.) I, Aphrodeitos, have signed. (6th h.) I, Dionysios, have signed.

berkeley:231553.t: P.Tebt., II.331. Petition to the Strategos
berkeley:231553.c: Akous, Son of Herakleos of Tebtunis, petitions the strategos complaining about a violent robbery. ; Translation: To Andromachos, strategos of the division of Polemon of the Arsinoite nome, from Akous son of Herakleos of the village of Tebtunis. On the first day of the present month Thoth Orsenouphis and Poueris, both sons of Mieus, and Theon and Sarapas, both sons of Chairas, and Poueris son of Ptollion and Maron son of Orseus and O…sautos son of Protas made a bold attack upon my house in the village … at the gateway, and when I was parleying with them belabored me with blows on every limb of

berkeley:231554.t: P.Tebt., II.308. Receipt for price of papyrus
berkeley:231554.c: Ammonios and Theon acknowledge receipt of the price (not stated) for papyrus from Petesouchos, son of Petesouchos and priest of Tebtunis. ; Translation: The 15th year of Aurelius Antoninus Caesar the Lord, Hathyr 13. Petesouchos son of Petesouchos, priest of Tebtunis, has paid to Ammonios and Theon, lessees of marshes and desert shore in the division of Polemon, the price of 20,000 papyrus stalks at Ibion Argaiou, which he has transported to Tebtunis by Herakleides, the brother of Ammonios.

berkeley:231555.t: P.Tebt., II.340. Declarations of grain revenue
berkeley:231555.c: Three declarations of grain revenue (in this case, specifically, wheat) from Antes and Thoteos, addressed to Flavius Heracleon, pasted together (tomos sunkollesimos). ; Translation: To Flavius Herakleon, strategos of the Mendesian nome, from Antes and Thoteus, grain-receivers of Hermopolis in the Hermopolite toparchy. The summary of the wheat measured to us from the produce of the past 14th year in accordance with the monthly account of Mesore by the collectors of Kellis for the village-dues is eight and a half artabas of unsifted wheat, total 8 1/2 art., which are stored at the granary under

berkeley:231558.c: Lyrics addressed by Helen of Troy to her husband Menelaos; an elaborate lyrical description of woodland solitude; 2 epigrammatic couplets concerning the passion of love; and other fragments.

berkeley:231559.t: P.Tebt., I.1; Page, D.L. Gr.lit.pap., I.92; Plate: P.Tebt. I.p1. I; Plate: Roberts, C.H. Gr. Lit. hands, pl. 7. no. 1606. Anthology : fragments
berkeley:231559.c: Lyrics addressed by Helen of Troy to her husband Menelaos; an elaborate lyrical description of woodland solitude; and 2 epigrammatic couplets concerning the passion of love. ; Translation: (Lines 1-4) O sweet delight didst thou seem to me, when thou lovedst me, when with hostile spear thou didst sack the Phrygians' city, desiring to take me only as thy spouse back to thy native land; but now, heartless one, wilt thou depart, leaving me a lonely wife, for whom went out the band of the Danaids, for whose sake Artemis carried off the unwed maid, Agamemnon's victim? berkeley:231560.t: P.Tebt., II.307. Tax receipt for sacrificial calf.
berkeley:231560.c: Receipt of payment for the tax upon a calf offered in sacrifice made by the priests of Tebtunis, Egypt, to Apion (Nomarches of the Arsinoite Nome). ; Translation: The 16th year of Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augusti and Publius Septimius Geta Caesar Augustus, Tybi 30. Paid to Apion, Nomarches of the Arsinoite nome, through Shpyris also called Theon, assistant, for the tenth upon calves by the priests of the village of Tebtunis, twenty drachmas, that is, 20 dr.

berkeley:231561.t: P.Tebt., I.39; Hunt, A.S. Sel.pap., v. 2, no. 276. Petition from Apollodoros to Menches
berkeley:231561.c: The oil-seller Apollodoros complains to Menches, village scribe, about two assaults by oil smugglers. ; Translation: To Menches, village scribe of Kerkeosiris, from Apollodoros, the contractor for the distribution of and the tax upon oil at the said village for the 4th year. I have already presented a memorandum to Polemon, the Epistates of the village, concerning my discovery on the 27th of Phaophi that there was at the house of Sisois son of Senapynchis in the shrine of Thoeris here a quantity of contraband oil. I immediately took Trychambos, the agent of the oikonomos who had been sent for

berkeley:231562.t: P.Tebt., II.421; Hunt, A.S. Sel.pap., v. 1, no. 135. Apion's letter : Theogonis, Egypt, to Didymos
berkeley:231562.c: Letter from Apion to Didymos, telling him that his sister is ill, and urging him t come to Theogonis at once. ; Translation: Apion to Didymos, greeting. Put off everything, and come to me immediately upon receiving this letter of mine, as your sister is sick. And when you come, bring the white tunic of hers that you have, but the turquoise one do not bring; but if you wish to sell it, sell it, if you wish to let your daughter have it, do so. But do not neglect her in any way, and do not trouble your wife or children, and when you come, come to Theogonis. I pray for your health.

berkeley:231563.t: P.Tebt., I.49; Chrest. Mitt., no. 19; Hengstl, J. Griechische papyri, no. 128. Petition from Apollophanes to Menches
berkeley:231563.c: Apollophanes complains to Menches, village Scribe of Kerkeosiris, that his plot of crown land had been flooded by his neighbor Nikon. ; Translation: To Menches, komogrammateus of Kerkeosiris, from Apollophanes son of Dionysodoros, cultivator of Crown land from the same village. On the 20th of Phaophi in the 5th year Nikon son of Amenneus, an inhabitant of the said village, let out the water on his own land and flooded 2 1/4 arouras of the Crown land belonging to me, which was then being ploughed, with the result that they were completely (ruined) and I suffered damage amounting to 20 artabas o

berkeley:231564.t: P.Tebt., I.10; Hunt, A.S. Sel.pap., v. 2, no. 339; U. Chrest. Wilck, no. 160; White, J. L. Light from ancient letters, no. 44; Plate: P.Tebt. I, Pl. V. Official letter from Asklepiades
berkeley:231564.c: Asklepiades informs Marres of Menches' renewed appointment as komogrammateus (village secretary) of Kerkeosiris. ; Translation: Asklepiades to Marres, greeting. Menches having been appointed village scribe of Kerkeosiris on the understanding that he shall cultivate at his own expense ten arouras of the land in the neighborhood of the village which has been reported as unproductive at a rent of fifty artabas, which he shall pay annually from the 52nd year to the Crown in full or shall measure out the deficiency from his private means, give to him the papers of his office and take care that the

berkeley:231565.t: P.Tebt., II.665; SB, XVIII, no. 13366. Penthemeros certificate
berkeley:231565.c: Certificate that Orseus, son of Psosneus and Tarm( ), performed his five days of dike corvee. ; Translation: Year seven of Imperator Caesar Nerva Trajanus Augustus Germanicus Dacicus. Has performed for five days for work on dykes for the same seventh year in the Hermoithes canal, on behalf of Tebtunis, (2nd h.) Orseus, son of Psosneus the son of Orseus, his mother is Tarm( ). (3rd h.) I, Aphrodeitos, have signed. (4th h.) I, Sokrates, have signed. (5th h.) I, Potamon, have signed. (6th h.) I Ptolemaios, have signed.

berkeley:231566.c: Part of an astrological treatise, being occupied with the connection between the heavenly bodies and various trades.

berkeley:231567.t: P.Tebt., II.269; P.Tebt., VI.1162. Prose work
berkeley:231567.c: The mention of the Sophists in the fragments suggests that this prose work was a philosophical treatise, unidentified.

berkeley:231568.t: P.Tebt., II.287; Chrest. Wilck., no. 251. Proceedings of a trial
berkeley:231568.c: Proceedings before Severianus, possibly the prefect, regarding an appeal made by the fullers and dyers of the Fayyum against an official who allegedly exacted an undue amount for the tax upon their respective trades. ; Translation: (…) in the … year of Antoninus and Verus the Lords Augusti, the fullers ad dyers from the Arsinoite nome having been summoned and having appeared, Longinus, advocate, said: "Of these men some are fullers and other dyers by trade, and for the tax on trades 1092 drachmas yearly are paid by the fullers and 1088 by the dyers according to tariff and custom. A certain Max

berkeley:231569.t: P.Tebt., II.286; Chrest. Mitt., no. 83. Proceedings of a trial : copy
berkeley:231569.c: Copy of the proceedings of a trial before the hypomnematographos Julius Theon regarding the ownership of a house. It cites the verdict of a previous trial (131 A.D.) which is based upon a rescript of the Emperor Hadrian, cited verbatim (lines 4-9). ; Translation: Extract from a rescript of the deified Hadrian. The 6th year of Hadrianus Caesar the Lord, Hathyr 17, Apollonides against Claudius Antoninus. berkeley:231575.t: P.Tebt., II.315; Hunt, A.S. Sel.pap. v. 1, no. 127; Chrest. Wilck., no. 71. Private letter concerning temple accounts
berkeley:231575.c: The unknown sender warns the addressee (possibly a temple priest) that an inspector was about to arrive, and promises to take care that he gets through the inspection. ; Translation: N.N. to his dearest N.N., greeting. I have sent you other letters about the 6 robes of Pyrrhos and the 2 cloaks of N.N. telling you to send them to me at any cost, and I am now writing in haste to prevent your being anxious, for I will see that you are not worried. You must know that an inspector of finance in the temples has arrived and intends to go to your division also. Do not be disturbed on this account, as

berkeley:231576.c: Probably an extract or summary of an extended work describing the effects of the position of the planets. ; Translation: If in addition Mercury is in conjunction, and Saturn is irregularly situated, … from an unfavorable position; if at the same time Mars is in opposition to Saturn, the aforesaid position being maintained (he will destroy?) profits of transactions. Saturn in triangular relation to Mars signifies (bad) fortune. Jupiter in triangular relation to Mars or in conjunction makes great kingdoms and empires. Venus in conjunction with Mars causes fornications and adulteries; if in addit

berkeley:231577.c: Astronomical work containing the daily motion of the moon during the Egyptian month of Mecheir.

berkeley:231578.t: P.Tebt., II.274; Neugebauer, O. "Egyptian planetary texts," Transactions Amer. Philos. Soc n.s. 72 (1942) p. 209-250 (text, especially 241ff) and plate 7. Astronomical calendar
berkeley:231578.c: Papyrus fragments of an astronomical calendar, recording the movements of heavenly bodies with reference to the signs of the Zodiac.

berkeley:231579.t: P.Tebt., II.326; Chrest. Mitt., no. 325,. Petition to the Prefect
berkeley:231579.c: Aurelia Sarapias petitions the prefect Juvenius Genialis to have her brother appointed guardian of her daughter. ; Translation: To Juvenius Genialis, his highness the prefect of Egypt, from Aurelia Sarapias, of Antinoe. On behalf of my orphan daughter who is under age, my lord prefect, I make this supplication and take refuge in your power. My husband Aurelius Paulus, of Antinoe, departed this life intestate, leaving our daughter, called Paulina, quite young. With regard therefore to the guardianship and administration of the child's property, having found that my own brother, Aurelius Sarapio

berkeley:231580.t: P.Tebt., II.333; Chrest. Mitt., no. 115. Petition to the Centurion
berkeley:231580.c: Aurelia Tisais, daughter of Kalibalis and Tais, petitions Julius Marcellinus, centurion, stating that her father and brother had disappeared on a hunting trip. ; Translation: To Aurelius Julius Marcellinus, centurion, from Aurelia Tisais, whose mother is Tais, formerly styled as an inhabitant of the village of Tebtunis in the division of Polemon. My father Kalabalis, Sir, who is a hunter, set off with my brother Neilos as long ago as the 3rd of the present month to hunt hares, and up to this time they have not returned. I therefore suspect that they have met with some accident, and I present t

berkeley:231581.t: P.Tebt., II.666; SB, XVIII, no. 13363. Penthemeros certificate
berkeley:231581.c: Certificate that Herakles, son of Horos and Tenapeis, performed his five days of dike corvee. ; Translation: Year two of Imperator Caesar Nerva Trajanus Augustus Germanicus. Has performed for five days for work on dikes for the same second year on the new dyke of the canal, (2nd h.) on behalf of Tebtunis, Herakles son of Horos the son of Herakles, his mother is Tenapeis. (3rd h.) I, Maron, katasporeus, have signed. (4th h.) I, Eudaimon, antigrapheus of (the office of) the strategos, have signed. (5th h.) I, Aphrodeitos, have signed.

berkeley:231582.t: P.Tebt., I.68. Register of the crops of crown lands
berkeley:231582.c: Register of the various crops on crown lands at Kerkeosiris in 117/116 B.C., with statement of the amounts of rent due to the crown.

berkeley:231584.t: P.Tebt., II.378; Lines 1-5: Chrest. Mitt., no. 326. Lease of land : signed by lessee
berkeley:231584.c: Aurelius Demetrios expresses his will to enter into an agreement with Aurelius Sarapammon and Aurelia Herakleia regarding the lease of a half share of a plot of land at Theogonis. ; Translation: To Aurelius Sarapammon, who is past his prime, and Aurelia Heraklia acting without a guardian, both children of Heron, from …is, Sarapammon having as curatrix his sister the aforesaid Heraklia, from Aurelius Demetrios, however he is styled. I wish to lease from you the half share owned by you at the village of Theogonis of nine grain-bearing arouras in one parcel, which formerly were leased to Heron, f

berkeley:231585.c: Aurelius Demetrios expresses his will to enter into an agreement with Aurelius Sarapammon and Aurelia Herakleia regarding the lease of a half share of a plot of land at Theogonis.

berkeley:231586.t: P.Tebt., II.420. Aurelius Sarapion's letter : to Polion and Diogenes
berkeley:231586.c: Letter from Aurelius Sarapion to his brother Polion and his father Diogenes, asking for financial help. ; Translation: Aurelius Sarapion to Polion his brother and Diogenes his father, very many greetings. You know that I am blameless, and you went away from me for no reason without giving me money. I bought two rolls of papyrus for the lists of the grain-dues (?) of the Basilikos Grammateus, and paid another 28 drachmas to the Basilikos Grammateus himself for the agreement concerning the unirrigated land. Therefore regarding this as a necessity use your best endeavors and send me my 52 drachma

berkeley:231587.c: Fragments of a census return by a woman to the strategos Nearchos, and to others including the obscure official called amphodarch, by a woman.

berkeley:231588.t: P.Tebt., II.449. Chaireas' letter to his son Kronion

berkeley:231589.c: Chaireas informs the addressee (whose name is lost in a lacuna) about some problems regarding the circumcision of a boy. ; Translation: Chaireas to his most honored Ma…, very many greetings. I believe that you are aware how much trouble I had in getting the circumcision through, owing to the high-priest's desire to see the boy, but by means of the good offices of our friends we achieved it. Good-bye, my brother. Salute Kronion and all his household. You will oblige me by sending the cloths, as I am in a hurry, and get me three matia of dried coriander and a measure of cumin, and send them to m

berkeley:231590.t: P.Tebt., II.301; C.P.Gr., v. 2, no. 64 (with plate). Declaration of death
berkeley:231590.c: Chairemon and Maron inform Horos, village scribe of Tebtunis, of the death of a person (name lost in lacuna). ; Translation: To Horos, komogrammateus of Tebtunis, from Chairemon son of Panomieus, priest of Isis and Serapis, of the village of Sobthis in the Herakleopolite nome, and from Maron son of Pakebkis son of Zosimus, exempted priest of the famous temple at the village of Tebtunis, both guardians of … ion son of Pakebkis, likewise priest of the said famous temple. …ion died in the present month Choiak of the present 31st year of Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Caesar the Lord, and I request t

berkeley:231591.t: P.Tebt., I.25, lines 1-7. Conclusion of an official letter
berkeley:231591.c: Conclusion of an official letter, warning the addressees not to take sides with persons working against the profit of the crown.

berkeley:231593.c: Receipt for payment of customs duties of 1 and 2 percent upon a donkey laden with 6 jars of wine. ; Translation: Aurelius Ploutammon has paid through the custom-house of Kaine the tax of 1/100 and 1/50 on importing upon one donkey six jars of wine. The 5th year, Phamenoth the fifth, 5th.

berkeley:231594.t: P.Tebt., II.668; SB, XVIII, no. 13362. Penthemeros certificate
berkeley:231594.c: Certificate that Herakles, son of Horos and Tenapeis, performed his five days of dike corvee. ; Translation: Year twelve of Imperator Caesar Domitianus Augustus Germanicus. Has performed for five days for work on dikes for the same twelfth year in the Hermoithes canal, (2nd h.) on behalf of Tebtunis, Herakles, son of Horos the son of Herakles, his mother is Tenapeis. (3rd h.) I, Dionysios, have signed. (4th h.) I, N.N., have signed. (5th h.) I, N.N., have signed. (6th h.) I, Aprhodeitos, have signed.

berkeley:231595.t: P.Tebt., II.412; Hunt, A.S. Sel.pap., v. 1, no. 128. Damas' letter : to his sister Artemidora
berkeley:231595.c: Damas asks his sister Artemidora to meet him at the Metropolis (i.e., Arsinoe) at the New Year. ; Translation: Damas, assistant, to Artemidora my sister, greeting. Before all else I make supplication for you every day. Please come up to the metropolis at the New Year, since I also am coming up to the city. Salute your mother and your father. I pray for your health.

berkeley:231596.t: P.Tebt., II.298; Chrest. Wilck., no.90. Declaration of priests and revenues of the temple at Tebtunis
berkeley:231596.c: List of priests of Soknebtunis exempt from poll-tax, and of payments in money and kind to the temple, some in connection with the sacred crocodiles at Tebtunis; and a list of revenues from property cultivated by the priests. ; Translation: To Apollonios, strategos of the division of Polemon in the Arsinoite nome, from Pakebkis son of Phanesis and Marepsemis son of Marenkaimis and Pakebkis son of Onnophris, all three stolistai, and Harpokration son of Marepsemis and Marsisouchos son of Onnophris and Marepsemis son of Marepsemis and Marsisouchos son of Pakebkis and Psenkebkis son of Pakebkis, al

berkeley:231597.t: P.Tebt., I.45; Chrest. Mitt., no. 40. Petition of Demas
berkeley:231597.c: Petition from Demas to Menches, the village scribe, complaining of a raid on his home by a band of marauders, headed by Pyrrhichus, son of Dionysios, and reporting which items were stolen on the occasion. ; Translation: To Menches, komogrammateus of Kerkeosiris, from Demas son of Sentheus, cultivator of Crown land and assistant for the cultivators of the said village. On the 8th of Mesore in the 4th year while I was engaged with the said cultivators in the collection of the sums owing for the leases of the same year, Pyrrhichos son of Dionysios, one of the katoikoi hippeis, and Herakleios son

berkeley:231598.t: P.Tebt., II.267. De falsa legatione : section 293-295
berkeley:231598.c: A short section of oration of Demosthenes, known from its Latin title as De falsa legatione.

berkeley:231599.t: P.Tebt., II.268; Eisenhut, W. Eph.bell.Tro., p. 134-139; Plate: P.Tebt., II, pl. II. Trojan War. Book 4, 9-15
berkeley:231599.c: Known hitherto only in a Latin version, this is a substantial fragment of the lost Greek original of Dictys Cretensis' Ephemeris belli Troiani.

berkeley:231600.t: P.Tebt., II.394. Receipt for payment of wheat
berkeley:231600.c: Didymos, also called Louris, acknowledges the receipt of money of 8 1/2 artabas for wheat for the military from the buyer Lysimachos, through the agency of a bank of Kerkesephis. ; Translation: Didumos also called Lourios, son of Lusimachos, to Lysimachos son of Pasion, greeting. I have received from you the price of bought wheat which you have deducted from the public bank from the credit of Ptolema daughter of Didymos, at Kerkesephis, 5 1/4 artabas of wheat, and from the credit of Tamystha daughter of Lysimachos, at Tebtunis, 1 1/2 artabas, and at Kerkeosiris likewise 1 1/2. Together the tot

berkeley:231601.c: Diodoros and partners, farmers of the crown tax of Theogonis, acknowledge receipt payments for the crown tax from Aion. ; Translation: Diodoros and partners, praktors of the crown-tax of the village of Theogonis, to Aion son of Apynchis, greeting. We have received from you for crown-tax of the 22nd (?) year, for the account of Hathyr 4 drachmas, Tybi 4 drachmas, Mecheir 16 obols, Pharmouthi 12 obols, Payni 16 obols, Mesore 16 obols, Phaophi 12 obols.

berkeley:231602.t: P.Tebt., I.28. Official letter from Dioskourides and Amenneus
berkeley:231602.c: Letter concerns the wrong-doings of a group of komogrammateis (village secretaries) with regard to their duties in the fiscal administration of land. These are detailed in an appended letter (probably P.Tebt.24). ; Translation: Dioskourides and Amenneus to Ptolemaios, greeting. Some of the hindrances placed in the way of the performance of our work through the insolent conduct of the komogrammateis in the nome, and how further in Mesore of the (52nd?) year, when we visited various places in the nome, having been appointed for this duty and wishing to inquire into the reports sent from the nome

berkeley:231603.t: P.Tebt., II.366; Chrest. Wilck., no. 371. Receipt for payments in kind
berkeley:231603.c: Ponnis and Eutychos, collectors of grain at Tebtunis, acknowledge having received various payments of wheat for various land taxes. Two of the taxpayers are women. ; Translation: The 28th year of Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Caesar the Lord, Payni 30. We, Ponnis son of Zoilos and Eutychos son of Koumaris and partners, (sitologoi) of the village of Tebtunis, have had measured to us from the produce of the said year by smoothed public measure to the account of Eutychos son of Hermes for the tax on cleruchs 14 1/8 artabas of wheat, and by Taarmiysis daughter of Pakebkis for the tax on cleru

berkeley:231604.t: P.Tebt., I.18. Official letter from Polemon
berkeley:231604.c: Polemon notifies Menches, the village secretary, of his arrival in Kerkeosiris, and tells Menches to join him to Berenikis ; Translation: Polemon to Menches, greeting. Since we are coming at dawn on the 29th, see that all the debts due to you and to the cultivators are in order on that day. You will set out for Berenikis with me with regard to the matter about which you wrote to me and in order that the report may not … Goodbye.

berkeley:231605.t: P.Tebt., III.772. Petition of Nechembes to Asklepiades
berkeley:231605.c: Nechembes, a tax farmer, petitions to Asklepiades (Nomarches), complaining that owing to damage caused by locusts owners of vineyards had refused to pay their dues to him, which had led to his arrest. ; Translation: To Asklepiades, nomarches, from Nechembes. After I had contracted for the tax of the sixth for (Arsinoe) Philadelphos in the division of Herakleides for the 10th year, there was an incursion of locusts which destroyed everything, what was saved being carried off by the owners without payment of the sixth. I have consequently been wrongfully arrested for this. You will therefore do

berkeley:231606.t: P.Tebt., I.21. Official letter from Polemon
berkeley:231606.c: Polemon informs Polemon that a collector had been instructed to stop operations at Kerkeosiris for the moment. ; Translation: Polemon to Polemon, greeting. I have written to Artemidoros the collector to stop work at Kerkeosiris until he proceeds to the city, and that Aristippos will come to an understanding with him. Do not therefore run away from anybody, for at present you have no produce. If he gives you trouble go up with him. Good-bye. The 3rd year, Choiak 4. (Addressed on the verso) To Polemon.

berkeley:231607.t: P.Tebt., I.17; Chrest. Wilck., no. 165; Hengstl, J. Griech. Pap., no. 15; White, J.L. Light from ancient letters, no. 48. Official letter from Polemon
berkeley:231607.c: Polemon announces to Menches the approach of a high official and warns Menches to have his accounts in order. ; Translation: Polemon to Menches, greeting. As it is decided that the epimeletes should proceed at daybreak on the 15th to Berenikis and on the 16th pass by the village on the way to Theogonis, endeavor to have all arrears owing from the neighborhood of the village in order, so that you may not detain him and thus incur no little expense. Good-bye. The 3rd year, Payni 11. (Addressed on the verso) To Menches, village scribe

berkeley:231608.t: P.Tebt., I.20. Official letter from Polemon
berkeley:231608.c: Polemon informs Menches that he sent a certain Harachthes as his substitute to a gathering of village secretaries asking Menches to introduce him and to pay him every attention. ; Translation: Polemon to Menches, greeting and good health. I have sent Harachthes to be with the komogrammateis until I come. You will do me a favor by personally introducing him and looking after them (him?), and in regard to the additions to the revenue letting him to nothing without your assistance, and if accounts are demanded consider that you have full powers until my arrival. Take care of yourself so as to rem

berkeley:231609.t: P.Tebt., I.19; White, J.L. Light from ancient letters, no. 49. Official letter from Polemon
berkeley:231609.c: Polemon urges his "brother" Menches to hasten the collection of the taxes. ; Translation: (2nd h.) Received in the 3rd year, Pachon [..]. (1st h.) Polemon to Menches his brother, greeting. I received what you wrote to me, and as for the cultivators whom you said you were sending, I do not require them. Asklepiades has pressed on matters and has imposed in addition to the proper amount 1000 artabas of wheat more, besides money, so I am anxious to make haste. Regarding the komogrammateis whom you mention, they will hardly depart until the 25th. You will be right in not diminishing the report com

berkeley:231610.c: Pnepheros, farmer of the taxes on beer and natron (salt) of Kerkeosiris, petitions the Basilikos Grammateus asking to be put under his protection; the Basilikos Grammateus subscribed to the petition and forwarded it to Menches ; Translation: (3rd h.) Received in the 53rd year, Tybi 15. (1st h.) To Amenneus, Basilikos Grammateus, from Pnepheros son of Paous, contractor for the taxes on beer and natron at Kerkeosiris in the division of Polemon for the 53rd year. Having received certain information that the inhabitants of the village are with one accord claiming your protection, and being myself

berkeley:231611.t: P.Tebt., II.684; Montanari, F. La Parola del Passato 208 (1983), p. 20-28. Olympian odes 9, 109-114 and 10, lines 1-12
berkeley:231611.c: Portions of lines from the 9th and 10th Olympian odes of Pindar.

berkeley:231612.c: Two copies of petitions: the first (lines 1-16) is from Phienous, and concerns her ownership of a farmstead at Alexandria; the second (lines 17-19) preserves only the first three lines of a petition of her husband ; Translation: Phienous, wife of Apollonios, senator of Antinooupolis (?) petitions: "The farmstead called that of Ammonas at Alexandria belongs to me, having been given to me as part of my dowry by my father Hermaiskos in accordance with publicly registered contracts; and I have always had the ownership of it and lodged my claim of ownership with Kritonius, and he declared to Myron

berkeley:231613.t: P.Tebt., III.715. Official letter from Petosiris
berkeley:231613.c: Petosiris urges Paramonos and the harvest-guards to take care that security for the payment of the rent was exacted from the farmers who had removed their crops. ; Translation: Petosiris, village scribe of Oxyrhyncha, to Paramonos and the harvest-guards, greeting. I have heard about the removal of the Greek reeds to … before we have received the proper security for the rent … the epigraphe being excessive. As soon as you receive this letter [set a watch on?] the village until security is received from the proprietors. Good-bye. The xxth year, Pachon 24. For instance, Demas son of N.N. and Keph

berkeley:231614.t: P.Tebt., II.296; Chrest. Wilck., no. 79. Documentary text concerning the purchase of a priestly office
berkeley:231614.c: Document regarding the purchase of the priestly office of Prophetes by a copy of a letter ordering the strategos (civil governor) of the Hermopolite Nome to hand over the office (dated Feb. 9, 123 A.D.) and a copy of the receipt for the full sum paid for the office (6000 drachmae). ; Translation: … in accordance with the letter sent by him the total amount of the increase was received. The following is a copy of the letter: Horas (?) … to the strategos of the Hermopolite nome, greeting. I forward the petition of Harthotes son of Harthotes, which I have signed. As therein declared, he has been

berkeley:231615.c: Pherous, village scribe of Boubastos, undertakes to deliver to Bakchios and Poseidonios, both managers of the granary, 350 artabas of wheat within fifteen days. ; Translation: Pherous, komogrammateus of Boubastos, to Bakchios and Poseidonios, sitologoi, greeting. The three hundred and fifty, total 350, artabas of wheat returned for me in a report in the month Hathyr I will pay to you at the storehouse at Boubastos by the 15th of the said month, or I will forfeit one and a half times the aforesaid amount. Good-bye. The 20th year, Hathyr 1.

berkeley:231616.c: Possibly a copy of the official correspondence.

berkeley:231617.t: P.Tebt., II.409. Dorion's letter : to Akousilaos
berkeley:231617.c: Letter from Dorion to the dioiketes Akousilaos concerning certain he-asses (?) which the writer wished to procure for him. ; Translation: Dorion to Akousilaos the dioiketes, very many greetings and wishes for continued health. At the metropolis I gave you 12 drachmas and asked you to give them to Lysimachos and ask him on my behalf to send me at once 3 he-asses without blemish, for I knew that both Lysimachos and you had plenty of them. I asked you, dear friend, since I knew that it was convenient for you, and that I shall have fine animal without blemish and good-tempered with your help. Good

berkeley:231618.t: P.Tebt., I.3; Plate: P.Tebt.I, pl. II. Epigrams
berkeley:231618.c: A fragment of a collection of Alexandrine epigrams, including four elegiac poems of which the 2nd (lines 13-20) is by Alcaeus of Messene (fl. beginning of 2nd century B.C.)

berkeley:231619.t: P.Tebt., II.683; F. Montanari, 'Un 'nuovo' papiro dell'Ecuba di Euripide (P.Tebt. 683 Rect0)', Riv. Fil. Ist. Cl. 115 (1987), p. 24-32 and 441-443. Hecuba, lines 216-231
berkeley:231619.c: Sixteen lines now known to be from Euripides' play Hecuba; identified as such by W.S. Barrett. At one time erroneously identified as a prose work.

berkeley:231620.t: P.Tebt., I.85; Plate: P. L. Bat. 29, pl. I. Field-by-field register of land at Kerkeosiris
berkeley:231620.c: Eight continuous columns of a field-by-field register of land at Kerkeosiris, giving for each plot the geographical relationship to other plots, the name of the landholder and his patronymic, the fiscal category to which the plot belongs, the area, and the rent paid to the crown per aroura if any.

berkeley:231621.t: P.Tebt., II.285; Chrest. Mitt., no. 379; Riccobono, S. Fontes iuris romani Anteiustiniani, v. 1, no. 90; Oliver, J. H. Greek constitutions, doc. 280; Plate: Oliver, H. H. Greek constitutions, p. 547. Rescript of the Emperor Gordian
berkeley:231621.c: Short rescript (written answer) of the Emperor Gordian, directing that failure to register children should not deprive them of their right to legitimacy. ; Translation: The deified Gordian Augustus to Nero Pudens. The omission to register children does not render them illegitimate, if they are legitimate, nor, if there are actually registers, can they introduce outsiders into the family. July 8, in the consulship of Gordian and Aviola.

berkeley:231622.t: P.Tebt., II.270; Korte, A. Archiv fur papyrusforschung, v. 6 (1913-1920), p. 259, no. 492 (lines 2-6 only). Grammar
berkeley:231622.c: Possibly a fragment of a grammar; lines 2-6 contain a quotation from the Odyssey, book 18, line 130.

berkeley:231623.t: P.Tebt., I.2 (d verso). Greek mime : fragment
berkeley:231623.c: Appears to be part of a dialogue, from a mime.

berkeley:231624.t: P.Tebt., I.46; Seider, R. Palaographie, v. 3.1, p. 346-348; Chrest. Mitt., no. 41. Petition of Harmiysis to Menches
berkeley:231624.c: Petition from Harmiysis, a farmer of crown lands at Kerkeosiris, to Menches, village scribe of the same village, complaining of a raid on his home by Pyrrhichus, son of Dionysius, and other marauders, and reporting that items were stolen on this occasion. ; Translation: To Menches, komogrammateus of Kerkeosiris, from Harmiysis son of Sarapion, cultivator of Crown land and inhabitant of the same village. On the 8th of Mesore of the 4th year my house was invaded by Pyrrhichos son of Dionysios, one of the katoikoi hippeis, and Herakleios son of Poseidippos, inhabitant of the said village, with ma

berkeley:231626.t: P.Tebt., II.437. Letter from Harpaesis : to his sister Koupa
berkeley:231626.c: Harpaesis informs his sister Koupa on a variety of subjects.

berkeley:231627.t: P.Tebt., III.836. Receipt for payments in kind : copy
berkeley:231627.c: Copy of a receipt for payment of rent and the three-choinix tax for the village of Oxyrhyncha, made by Komoapis son of Onnophris. ; Translation: Copy of a receipt for grain measured at Eleusis. 6th year, Payni 8, from Sokrates, sitologos of the granary at Mouchis. Grain measured as rent out of the produce of the said year at Eleusis for Oxyrhyncha from Komoapis son of Onnophris, for rent 17 artabas of pure wheat, for the three-choinix tax 1 1/4 art.

berkeley:231628.t: P.Tebt., II.434; Chrest. Mitt., no. 51. Petition from Harpochras
berkeley:231628.c: Conclusion of a petition from Harpochras to probably a strategos.

berkeley:231629.t: P.Tebt., I.44; Chrest. Wilck. No. 118. Totti, M. Ausgewahlte Texte der Isis und Sarapis-Religion, no. 69. Petition from Haryotes to Menches
berkeley:231629.c: Haryotes complains of an attack made upon him at the temple of Isis. ; Translation: To Menches, komogrammateus of Kerkeosiris, from Haryotes son of Phaesis, cultivator of Crown land and an inhabitant of the said village. While I was in the great temple of Isis here for devotional purposes on account of the sickness from which I am suffering, on the 23rd of Pachon in the 3rd year Horos son of Haryotes, a resident in the aforesaid temple of Isis, picked a quarrel with me, and beginning with abuse and unseemly behavior he at last fell upon me and gave me many blows with the staff which he was car

berkeley:231630.t: P.Tebt., II.369. Receipt for payment in kind
berkeley:231630.c: Herakles and partner sitologoi (collectors of grain) of Kerkesis acknowledge receipt of wheat to the account of Thermoutharion. ; Translation: The eleventh year of Imperator Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, Payni 14. We, Herakles son of Deios and partners, sitologi of the village of Kerkesis, have had measured to us from the produce of the same year to the account of Thermoutharion, freedwoman of Soterichos, through Eutychos, two-thirds and one twenty-fourth of an artaba of bought wheat, by smoothed public measure, total 17/24 artabas of wheat.

berkeley:231631.t: P.Tebt., III.712. Official letter of Herakleides : to elders of the farmers of Areos Kome
berkeley:231631.c: Herakleides complains to the elders of the farmers at Areos Kome for waiting too long regarding steps to be taken against Petesokonouris. Meaning and nature of action is not clear. ; Translation: Herakleides to Horos and Petenouris and the elders of the cultivators, greeting. In accordance with your request that I should do nothing further up to the 25th until I met Petesokonouris, having now waited instead of the 25th till the 5th of Mecheir without any of you having brought me to …, even so, notwithstanding my annoyance I have had patience and written to you: even now, if you have made any d

berkeley:231632.c: Beginning of a copy of a census declaration of Heras, daughter of Lysimachos of Arsinoe, Egypt. ; Translation: Copy of a registration. To Maximus also called Nearchos, strategos, and Herakleides, Basilikos grammateus of the division of Herakleides in the Arsinoite nome, and to Sabinos and Antoninus, scribes of the metropolis, and to the amphodarch and registrar of the Linen-factories' quarter, from Heras daughter of Lysimachos son of Herodion, her mother being Tamystha, enrolled in the quarter of the Hawk-shrine of Apollonios, with my guardian my kinsman Herakleides son of Patron. I own in the

berkeley:231633.t: P.Tebt., II.679; Johnson, "A botanical papyrus with illustrations," Archiv fur die Geschichte der Naturwissenschaften und der Technik, v. 4 (1912-1913), p.403-408, and plate I-II. Herbal
berkeley:231633.c: Fragment of an illustrated herbal, consisting of a treatise on the medical properties of plants.

berkeley:231635.c: Fragments of a work written in non-Homeric hexameters. Possibly from Hesiod's Catalog of women, a work popular in Egypt, as the passage relates to King Minos of Crete, his love for women, and the birth of a child, the Minotaur, whose mother was Pasiphae. Only fragments survive of the catalog of women.

berkeley:231641.t: P.Tebt., II.271; Schubart, W. Goettingische gelehrte Anzeigen 1908, p. 189-190. Catalog of women
berkeley:231641.c: Fragment of Hesiod's Catalog of women (the Tyro passage); lines 2-3 are identical to Homer's Odyssey, Book 2, lines 249-250.

berkeley:231649.t: P.Tebt., II.425; P.Tebt., VI.1166. Iliad. Book 1, lines 311-327

berkeley:231650.c: Apollonios orders Achilles to transfer payments from fishermen to Onnophris, a priest. ; Translation: Apollonios to Achilles, greeting. Deduct from the fishermen the regular day of … in Phaophi and give the payments to Onnophris the priest, as usual, and make out a receipt. And notify us also whatever disposition you make about … Goodbye. The 13th year, Phaophi 21.

berkeley:231656.c: Few letters from miscellaneous lines of the Iliad, Book 2, with occasional accents and breathings.

berkeley:231658.t: P.Tebt., II.302; Chrest. Wilck., no. 368. Petition to the prefect
berkeley:231658.c: A petition to a prefect whose name is lost from priests of Soknebtunis with regard to their right to cultivate land at Tebtunis, formerly temple land, but recently converted to crown land ; Translation: To N.N., the lord prefect, from NN.NN. and the rest of the hereditary priests of the famous temple of Soknebtunis also called Kronos, Isis, Sarapis, Harpokrates and the associated gods, situated at the village of Tebtunis in the division of Polemon of the Arsinoite nome. We have had assigned to us from the state instead of a subvention 500 1/4 arouras of grain land at the said village of Tebtun

berkeley:231665.t: P.Tebt., II.429; P.Tebt., VI.1165. Iliad. Book 13, lines 340-350, 356-375

berkeley:231666.c: Dionysios, Adamas (both holders of a 30 arouras cleruchic plot) and Poseidonios notify Philon (Archiphylakites) that their house had been entered and property stolen. ; Translation: The 21st year, Phaophi 11. To Philon, archiphylakites, from Dionysios and Adamas, 30-arouras-holders, and Poseidonios. On the night between the 10th and 11th of the aforesaid month certain persons climbed into our house, and coming into the vestibule, while our people were asleep in their chambers with the doors shut, went away with a grain-basket in the vestibule containing a half-artaba of barley worth 90 drachma

berkeley:231668.c: Fragments from the Odyssey, Book 1; a not very accurate text, with a new line inserted following 92.

berkeley:231669.c: Lines from Books 4 and 5 of the Odyssey, representing eccentricities common in Homeric texts from Ptolemaic Egypt.

berkeley:231670.c: Fragments of the Odyssey, Book 11, with occasional accents.

berkeley:231671.c: Fragment from the Odyssey, Book 24, with occasional accents.

berkeley:231672.t: P.Tebt., I.51. Petition from Horos : to Menches
berkeley:231672.c: The petition concerns a nursing contract (lines 7-8) and relates misbehavior from the woman. ; Translation: To Menches, komogrammateus of Kerkeosiris, from Horos, son of Petechon, king's farmer of the area of the same (village). Inasmuch as I am living with ]thonis, daughter of T[…]os, from the area of the same village in accordance with an Egyptian boarding contract, and as I am providing the same all the necessities according to the ability of my resources…

berkeley:231673.c: Circular letter from the Horos, royal secretary, to the topogrammateis and komogrammateis (local and village secretaries) of the Arsinoite Nome (modern Fayyum, Egypt) containing copies of correspondence from the dioiketes (finance minister) Eirenaios and concerning crop management. The letter includes a long letter censuring a certain Hermias for carelessness in this regard. ; Translation: (2nd hand) Received in the 4th year, Mecheir 10. (1st hand) Horos to the topogrammateis and komogrammateis, greeting. Appended is a copy of the letter from Eirenaios the king's cousin and dioiketes, concerni

berkeley:231674.t: P.Tebt., I.48. Chrest. Wilck., no. 409. White, L. Light from Ancient Letters, no. 50. Petition from Horos and the elders of the farmers : to Menches
berkeley:231674.c: Horos, Komarches of Kerkeosiris, and the elders of the farmers complain to the village scribe Menches about an attack upon them. ; Translation: To Menches, komogrammateus of Kerkeosiris, from Horos, komarches, and the elders of the cultivators of the said village. We signed an undertaking to Polemon the toparches that we would supply to the treasury by the 10th of Pachon 1500 artabas of wheat, and we have been working night and day to make up the aforesaid amount and also the 80 artabas of wheat for the supplies imposed in connection with the king's visit. On the 3rd of the month mentioned bel

berkeley:231675.t: P.Tebt., I.53. Petition of Horos: to Petesouchos
berkeley:231675.c: Horos, farmer of crown lands at Kerkeosiris, Egypt, petitions Petesouchos, successor to Menches as village secretary of the same village, complaining about the theft of 40 sheep for which he was responsible, by inhabitants of a neighboring village. ; Translation: To Petesouchos, komogrammateus of Kerkeosiris, from Horos son of Konnos, cultivator of Crown land and inhabitant of the said village. berkeley:231676.t: P.Tebt., II.293; Hunt, A.S. Sel.pap., v. 2, no. 338. Chrest. Wilck., no. 75. Declaration on oath concerning circumcision
berkeley:231676.c: Kronion, son of Pakebkis, and three other priests from Tebtunis, Egypt, declare on oath that an applicant for circumcision is of a priestly pedigree and fit for the rite. Three of the four declarants sign the oath. ; Translation: From Kronion, son of Pakebkis son of Harpokration, deputy prophetes, and from Maron son of Kronion son of Harpokration, and Maron son of Maron son of Marepsemis, and Pakebkis son of Kronion son of Psyphis, the three last being priests, all four from the famous exempted temple of the village Tebtunis. With regard to the application presented to you by Marepsemis son of

berkeley:231677.t: P.Tebt., III.823. Receipt of a shipping contractor
berkeley:231677.c: Ammonios, a shipping contractor, acknowledges the receipt of 5556 artabas for shipment to Alexandria. ; Translation: In the reign of Ptolemy son of Ptolemy and Arsinoe, gods Philopatores, the 21st year, Hathyr 2. Ammonios, contractor for the kerkouros of Polykrates, of … burden, acknowledges embarkation at the harbor of Kerke for conveyance to Alexandria to the royal granary, from the produce of the 20th year, through Bakchios and Ammonios, sitologoi of the store at Hiera Nesos, with the controllers, of five thousand five hundred and fifty-six artabas of olyra paid as rent and for transport by

berkeley:231678.c: Details concerning the owners and cultivators of land in the Fayyum, Egypt.

berkeley:231680.c: Liberalis orders Herakleos to pay 200 drachmas in return for barley. ; Translation: Liberalis to Herakleos, most dear, greetings. Give the two hundred drachmas to the people from whom you have received barley. Goodbye.

berkeley:231683.c: A list of holders of lands and crops at Kerkeosiris.

berkeley:231697.t: P.Tebt., I.142; P.Tebt., IV.1099; White, J.L. Light from Ancient Letters, no. 46. Official letter from Menches : to Horos
berkeley:231697.c: Menches informs Horos, the Basilikos Grammateus, about a strike of crown tenants at Kerkeosiris. ; Translation: Menches, komogrammateus of Kerkeosiris in the division of Polemon, to Horos, greeting. When I was in Ptolemais Euergetis for the delivery of the requested documents, we happened to hear that the crown tenants of the village had gone away to the temple at Narmouthis. I considered it right to make a supplementary report so that you know. Good-bye. The 4th year, Phaophi 20. (Addressed on the verso) To Horos.

berkeley:231698.c: Perhaps the remains of a medical work.

berkeley:231699.c: Fragment possibly from a scientific treatise.

berkeley:231703.c: Marres complains to Menches for not having given a relative of his the special treatment he deserved, and urges him to not repeat such behavior in the future. ; Translation: Marres to Menches, greeting. My kinsman Melas has appealed to me concerning an alleged injury from you obliging him to complain to Demetrios son of Niboitas. berkeley:231704.c: Official letter from Marres to Menches, forwarding a letter from the Basilikos Grammateus (royal scribe) concerning a change of ownership of a plot of cleruchic land. ; Translation: (2nd h.) Received in the 5th year, Phamenoth .. (1st h.) Marres to Menches, greeting. A copy is appended of the letter from Horos, Basilikos Grammateus, about the cession which he states has been made to Dionysios son of Dionysios by Menandros son of Pantauchos of a holding near Kerkeosiris. berkeley:231705.c: A series of medical recipes; a large number of them are for diseases of the eyes.

To Apollonios, epimeletes. Phanesis, komogrammateus of Koitai, having sent me the appended letter in which he declares that he has persuaded the crown cultivators of Dinnys, who were objecting to the land added by him, to accept on agreed terms the land they objected to, we thought it necessary to report to you in order that, if you think fit, you may give orders that arrangements be made for

berkeley:231709.c: Menches seeks reappointment as komogrammateus (village secretary) at Kerkeosiris, Egypt, promising to pay a certain amount of grains at the village. A certain Dorion adds 60 artabas to the amount promised by Menches. ; Translation: From Menches, village scribe of Kerkeosiris. On being appointed to the post of village scribe previously held by me I will pay at the village 50 artabas of wheat and 50 artabas of pulse, namely 20 artabas of lentils, 10 of bruised beans, 10 of peas, 6 of mixed seeds, 3 of mustard, 1 of parched pulse, total 50; total 100 artabas. berkeley:231710.c: Acknowledgement by Menches, village scribe of Kerkeosiris, Egypt, stating that he has received from Dorion 161 artabas of grains, and Dorion owes him further payments. ; Translation: Menches son of Petesouchos, village scribe of Kerkeosiris in the division of Polemon in the Arsinoite nome, to Dorion son of Eirenaios, one of the first friends. berkeley:231711.c: Draft of a letter from Menches (village scribe of Kerkeosiris) to Horos, probably the royal scribe, in which he reports about an attack upon the son of the village Epistates (superintendent). At the end of the letter follows in the same hand a note from Horos, royal scribe of Kerkeosiris. ; Translation: Menches, village scribe of Kerkeosiris, to Horos, greeting. I reported to you in another letter on the 3rd of the current month the case of Polemon who is performing the duties of Epistates of the village, how he was grossly insulted by Apollodoros and his son. These persons persisting in their

berkeley:231712.t: P.Tebt., I.14; Chrest. Mitt., no. 42. Menches' Official letter : to Horos : draft
berkeley:231712.c: Draft of an official letter from Menches, village scribe of Kerkeosiris, Egypt, to Horos, royal scribe of Kerkeosiris, informing him that he has taken requested measures regarding a judicial inquiry for murder and seizure of property against Heras, son of Petalos, inhabitant of Kerkeosiris. ; Translation: Menches, village scribe of Kerkeosiris in the division of Polemon, to Horos, greeting. berkeley:231714.t: P.Tebt., I.43; Chrest Mitt., no. 46; lines 43-44: C.Ord.Ptol., no. 56. Petition of Menches to the Sovereigns

You must know that Ammonios our late agent (?), being in the office of Amenneus the basilikos grammateus, has written to us concerning the detention of Aroteus the son of Petearphres by the basilikos grammateus for the survey of the village and the measurements; and he has written to me to join them. I have asked him to wait for me until the 21st. So so

berkeley:231716.c: Rough drafts of two official letters from Menches, village secretary of Kerkeosiris, Egypt, to Horos, probably the Basilikos Grammateus. Both letters report on matters related to an attack on Polemon, the Epistates (superintendent) of Kerkeosiris. ; Translation: To Horos, greeting. On the 1st of the current month at about the eleventh hour a disturbance occurred in the village, and on running out we found a crowd of the villagers who had come to the assistance of Polemon, who is performing the duties of Epistates of the village. When we inquired into the matter, they informed us that Apollodor

berkeley:231717.t: P.Tebt., I.8; Plate: P.Tebt., I, plate IV; JEA, v. 61, plate 24. Notes unidentified

berkeley:231718.t: P.Tebt., I.55. Witkowski, S. Epistulae privatae, no. 53. Official letter from Mousaios: to Menches
berkeley:231718.c: Mousaios writes to his 'brother' Menches, probably the village scribe of Kerkeosiris, Egypt, about various grains. ; Translation: Mousaios to his brother Menches, greeting and good health. Since I have decided to travel to Tebtunis on the 8th, I have determined to write to you. Your agent has brought to me one artaba of ami. You will therefore confer a favor on me by sending me two artabas of lentils and two artabas of fenugreek. For the rest take care of yourself, so as to keep in good health. Good-bye. I was engaged in company with my brother Mestasytmis also called Pates, son of Petemounis, in the cultivation of 12 arouras of

berkeley:231724.c: The strategos (civil governor) orders the Epistates of Tebtunis to send up two persons. ; Translation: To the Epistates of Tebtunis. Send up Galates and his wife, both children of Kronion, who are accused by Semele daughter of Akousilaos.

berkeley:231726.c: Pakebkis petitions Longinus, Decurion of the Arsinoite Nome, about an attack upon him and his brother by a certain Satornilus. ; Translation: To Longinus, decurion of the Arsinoite nome, from Pakebkis son of Onnophris from the village of Tebtunis, exempted priest of the famous temple in the village. On the 30th of the month Epeiph, when the hour was late, one Satorneilos, with a great many others, I know not why, having no complaint against us, picked a quarrel, going so far as to rush in with staves, and seizing my brother Onnophris they wounded him, so that his life is endangered in conseque

I have from you on deposit from hand to hand out of the house, from the public moneys which you administer, 120 drachmas, which I will repay whenever you choose, without any delay or excuse. The fifth year of Imperator Caesar Vespasianus Augustus, Epeiph 4.

My father Psoiphis son of Paopis and Asis of the said village, exempted priest of the said temple, died in the month Tybi of the present 14th year of Antoninus Caesar the Lord. berkeley:231729.t: P.Tebt., I.50; Chrest. Wilck., no. 329. Petition from Pasis : to Menches
berkeley:231729.c: Pasis complains to Menches that his neighbor, against an order from Menches himself, has still damned up the canal by which Pasis waters his plot of crown land, causing a loss of produce. ; Translation: To Menches, village scribe of Kerkeosiris, from Pasis son of Petesouchos, cultivator of crown land from the same village. It is an old-established custom to water the royal land belonging to me in the neighborhood of the said village by means of the royal conduit which passes through the adjacent crown and temple land of Lykos son of Zopyrion, and others. Now in the 2nd year during my absence f

berkeley:231730.t: P.Tebt., I.140 (desc. only). Account of expenses
berkeley:231730.c: Account of expenses connected with the notary office of Theogonis and Kerkethoeris.

berkeley:231731.c: Letter from Patron, resident of Oxyrhynchite Nome, chiefly dealing with private matters. ; Translation: Goodbye. The 2nd year, Tybi 30. Patron to --ippos, greeting. Ptolemaios the merchant's son has written to … his father of the way in which we instructed you about the 50 drachmas o as to make another loan (?) until our boat starts. Give him therefore my letter lest you lose the chance. I have written for you a copy of his letter to me and of what he writes to his father. He brings you some … lotus-fruit. Goodbye. The 2nd year, Tybi 30.

berkeley:231732.t: P.Tebt., II.411. Letter from Paulinus : to Heron
berkeley:231732.c: Paulinus informs Heron, his son, that the Epistrategos (civil governor) had made inquiries for him and urges him to come at once. ; Translation: Paulinus to his son Heron, greeting. Immediately upon receiving my letter come up instantly, for his highness the epistrategos has made several inquiries for you. He might even have proscribed you, had I not promised that you would be present today. Do not therefore fail; do not be disturbed however, for when you come you will know what it means. I pray for your good health. Pachon 3.

berkeley:231733.t: P.Tebt., I.29; Chrest. Mitt., no. 24. Official letter from Petesouchos : to the chrematistai
berkeley:231733.c: Petesouchos, village scribe of Kerkeosiris, petitions the chrematistai (Egyptian judges) for postponement of a pending trail against him. ; Translation: To the chrematistai whose clerk is Do[…] from Polemon also called Petesouchos, village scribe of Kerkeosiris in the division of Polemon. Akousilaos and Ptolemaios, both sons of Herakleides and inhabitants of the said village, have presented to me from you a copy of a petition alleging that I had defrauded them of some land, about which I too have presented to you a memorandum rebutting their charge. Since the proper time for the vintage(?) has

berkeley:231734.c: Register of land the revenue of which was set aside for a special, unknown purpose. ; Translation: The 7th year, from Petesouchos, village scribe of Kerkeosiris. It is reported that the land near the village which formerly belonged to Ptolemaios son of Philinos is in the (category of land) the produce of which is set aside, which land was brought under cultivation in the 49th year by Dionysios the supervisor and was cultivated in the 7th year by Peteskontis and his associates. The area is 16 1/2 arouras producing 20 (?) artabas.

berkeley:231735.t: P.Tebt., I.78; lines 1-12: Cuvigny, H. L'Arpentage par especes, p. 77. Register of land
berkeley:231735.c: Register of land the revenue of which was set aside for a special, unknown purpose. Below it is a royal oath vouching for the correctness of the statement. ; Translation: The .. year, from Petesouchos, village scribe of Kerkeosiris. List, yielded by the inquiry held by Horos the Basilikos Grammateus after the survey of the same year concerning the area sown of the land at Kerkeosiris which is in the category of the revenue which is set aside, stating also the several amounts in excess which result. The total amount reclaimed from the unprofitable land being 78 arouras, of this number 16 1/2 ar

berkeley:231736.t: P.Tebt., III.771. Petition from Petesouchos to the king and queen of Egypt
berkeley:231736.c: Petesouchos complains to the sovereigns of Egypt that he was being disturbed in the possession of his house at Oxyrhyncha by Stratonike, daughter of Ptolemaios, of Krokodilon Polis. ; Translation: To king Ptolemaios and Queen Kleopatra, his sister, motherloving gods, greeting from Petesouchos son of Petos, Crown cultivator from the village of Oxyrhyncha in the division of Polemon in the Arsinoite nome. I live in Kerkeosiris in the said nome, and there belongs to me in the aforesaid village of Oxyrhyncha a house inherited from my father, possessed by him for the period of his lifetime and by my

berkeley:231738.t: P.Tebt., I.47; Plate: P.Tebt., I, pl. VII. Petition to Menches
berkeley:231738.c: Petition from 2 or more farmers of crown land at Kerkeosiris to Menches, complaining of a raid on their home by Pyrrhichos and other marauders and reporting that items were stolen on this occasion ; Translation: (To Menches, komogrammateus of Kerkeosiris, from N.N. and N.N.,) cultivators of Crown land and inhabitants of the said village. On the 8th of Mesore of the 4th year as we were in the fields at work upon the land which we cultivate near the village, Pyrrhichos son of Dionysios, a catoecic cavalry-soldier, and Herakleios son of Poseidippos, an inhabitant of the said village, invaded our

berkeley:231741.c: Crown tenants at Oxyrhyncha petition to Phanias (Strategos and overseer of the revenues), asking for his protection against possible oppression by other officials. ; Translation: To Phanias, one of the first friends and strategos and overseer of the revenues, from the farmers of crown land at Oxyrhyncha. berkeley:231750.c: Chration acknowledges the repayment of a loan of 2448 silver drachmas by Thaesis. ; Translation: Year eight of Imperator Caesar Nerva Trajanus Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, Phaophi 21, in Theogonis of the division of Polemon in the Arsinoite nome. Chration, son of Horion, about forty-six years old, with a scar on his left shin, acknowledges to Thaesis, daughter of Kronion also called Psenkebkis the son of Marsisouchos, about forty-seven years old, with a scar on her right shin, acting with her guardian, her relative Marepsemis son of Marepsemis, about thirty-seven years old, with a scar on the

berkeley:231769.c: Asklepiades, sitologos for cavalry dues in the division of Polemon, petitions to Petosiris, village scribe of Oxyrhyncha, complaining about an attack upon him by attendants of the bath. ; Translation: To Petosiris, komogrammateus of Oxyrhyncha, from Asklepiades, sitologos for cavalry dues in the division of Polemon. On the .. of the present month, when I was bathing in the bath here, being seriously ill, after I had come out of the bath in an exhausted condition, Pasis son of Aretion and (blank) and (blank), attendants at the said bath, because he had 15 drachmas of silver seized my servant, w

berkeley:231770.t: P.Tebt., I.134 (desc. only). Petition of Herakleides : to Antaios
